grading_standard: All requested material parts required; abstention partial, contradiction incorrect. Grade semantics independent of support label. Unsupported guesses separately flagged. No cross-answer borrowing.

grades.question: How is the Conflict deck built, and what happens to unused Conflict cards?
grades.expected: Shuffle all four III cards at the bottom, five randomly dealt of nine II cards above, one randomly dealt of three I cards on top: ten total. Return unused cards to the box without looking.

observed.answer: Shuffle all four III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle the nine II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle the three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return the unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
observed.evidence: Setup: ‘face-down 10-card Conflict Deck’; return unused Conflict cards ‘without looking at them.’

grades.reason: Gives all three shuffled tiers, their used counts and order, and returns unused cards unseen.

grades.question: What are the starting score, Agents, troops and water for a human in a four-player game versus a three-player game?
grades.expected: Four players start at 1 VP; three at 0. Each has two Agents on Leader and third beside board, three troops in garrison with remaining nine in supply, and one water.

observed.answer: In four players, start at 1 VP; in three players, start at 0 VP. Both setups give a human two Agents on the Leader and a third (Swordmaster) beside the board, 12 troops total (three in the garrison and nine in supply), and 1 water.
observed.evidence: Setup: Score track ‘on the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0’; two Agents on Leader; 12 troop cubes; ‘Take 1 water.’

grades.reason: Distinguishes 1 versus 0 starting VP and supplies both Agent locations, 3/9 troop allocation and one water.

grades.question: Can you Reveal with Agents left, and can you later take an Agent turn in the same round? What cards supply Reveal effects and where do all played cards go?
grades.expected: May Reveal early; no more turns this phase after Reveal. Only cards remaining in hand and just revealed supply Reveal effects, not Agent-turn cards. Clean Up puts all Agent and Reveal cards in discard pile.

observed.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, but taking a Reveal turn ends your turns for the phase; you cannot take an Agent turn afterward that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed from the remaining hand, not Agent-played cards. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
observed.evidence: Player Turns: ‘Agent turns are optional’; ‘Once you’ve taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped’; Reveal effects are of ‘just-revealed cards only.’

grades.reason: Permits early Reveal, prohibits later turns, limits Reveal effects to remaining hand, and discards both groups at cleanup.

grades.question: May an Agent-turn card effect provide resources to pay the destination entry cost? How many Agents can one card send, and can a card without Agent icons be used?
grades.expected: Entry costs paid immediately before any card or space effects; cannot use later gains to pay entry. One card sends one Agent using one matching icon. No-icon card cannot be played on an Agent turn.

observed.answer: Before placement, you may play a legal Plot Intrigue and use resources it grants to pay the entry cost. Resources from the Agent card or destination effects occur after placement and cannot pay that same cost. One card sends only one Agent, using one chosen matching icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn.
observed.evidence: Player Turns: Plot effects before placement can join available resources; gains ‘only after placement’ cannot pay entry; ‘one card can’t send multiple Agents.’

grades.reason: Requires entry payment before Agent-card/space gains, sends one Agent with one icon, and excludes no-icon cards; the volunteered pre-entry Plot exception is supported.

grades.question: At a Combat space you recruit three troops this turn and already have four garrisoned. How many can deploy? What if the destination is not a Combat space, and where do recruited troops originate?
grades.expected: May deploy all three newly recruited plus at most two older garrison troops, five total. Normal deployment unavailable at noncombat space. Recruit from own supply into garrison; empty supply prevents recruiting.

observed.answer: At a Combat space, deploy the three troops recruited that turn plus at most two from the four already in your garrison, for five total. At a non-Combat space you cannot normally deploy. Recruited troops come from your supply and are put in your garrison until deployed.
observed.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: deploy ‘any or all units recruited during your current turn’ plus ‘up to two more’ from garrison; recruit from supply into garrison.

grades.reason: Allows three new plus at most two old troops, denies ordinary non-Combat deployment, and recruits from personal supply into garrison. Empty-supply consequences were not separately requested.

grades.question: How do you use a Spy Agent icon, Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence? Can the same Spy pay for both, and when must Gather Intelligence be chosen?
grades.expected: Spy Agent icon permits a connected space without recalling Spy. Infiltrate recalls own connected Spy to bypass another player Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls own connected Spy to draw, chosen immediately after placement before card/space effects. Same Spy cannot do both; separate Spies can.

observed.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to a space connected to a post where you have a Spy; it does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player’s Agent, but not your own. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy after placing your Agent to draw a card, and must be chosen immediately after placement before space or Agent-card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both; two different Spies can be used for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on one placement.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Spy Agent icon ‘do not recall’; Infiltrate bypasses another player; Gather Intelligence is decided ‘immediately after placing your Agent’; cannot recall same Spy for both.

grades.reason: Distinguishes Spy-icon access without recall, occupancy infiltration, and immediately post-placement intelligence; separate Spies can fund the two different effects.

grades.question: With two troops, one sandworm and four revealed swords, what is your strength? What if your final unit is removed? Can you participate in Combat Intrigue with no unit?
grades.expected: Strength 11 (2+2+3+4). No units means zero strength regardless swords. Without a unit cannot participate in Combat Intrigue.

observed.answer: Strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm 3, and four swords 4. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0, regardless of swords. With no unit in the Conflict, you are ineligible for Combat Intrigue.
observed.evidence: Strength: troop = 2, sandworm = 3, sword = 1; ‘must have at least one unit’; Combat Intrigue: player needs ‘at least one unit.’

grades.reason: Computes 11, makes strength zero on losing the final unit, and excludes unit-free Combat Intrigue participation.

grades.question: If you pass Combat Intrigue and an opponent then plays one, may you act again? When does the window close, and where do troops and sandworms go after rewards?
grades.expected: May act again after earlier pass; closes only when all involved players pass consecutively. Adjust strength for effects. After all rewards troops return to supply not garrison, sandworms to bank, Combat markers reset zero.

observed.answer: Yes. Passing once does not prevent acting again; the window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
observed.evidence: Combat Intrigue: ‘not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; close after consecutive passes; cleanup returns troops to supply and resets markers.

grades.reason: Allows acting after an earlier pass, requires consecutive passes to close, and returns troops to supply and worms to bank; also resets markers.

grades.question: Compare two players tied for first in a four-player Conflict with the same tie in a three-player Conflict. Who takes the Conflict card, and can a zero-strength player get a reward?
grades.expected: Each tied first gets second reward and nobody wins or takes card. In four-player game remaining players compete for third; in three-player game no further rewards. Zero strength never rewarded.

observed.answer: In both cases each of the two tied for first gets the second reward, and nobody takes the Conflict card. In a four-player game the remaining players compete for the third reward; in a three-player game there are no other rewards. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
observed.evidence: Combat ties: exactly two tied first in four players leaves others to compete for third; with three or fewer, no other rewards; nobody takes card; ‘0 strength receives no reward.’

grades.reason: Gives both tied leaders second rewards, no winner/card, four-player third-place competition versus no further three-player rewards, and no reward at zero.

grades.question: What does a sandworm do to rewards: do two sandworms quadruple them, can control or battle icons double, and how is a reward offering 3 spice for 1 VP handled?
grades.expected: One or more sandworms doubles, never quadruples. Control and battle icons do not double. Optional reward cost may be paid second time: 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2, not free second VP.

observed.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; multiple worms do not multiply the doubling further, so two worms do not quadruple rewards. Control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards cannot be doubled. If a reward is pay 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay 3 again for a second VP (or 6 spice for 2 VP).
observed.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘one or more sandworms, double’; control and battle icons cannot; may pay cost a second time.

grades.reason: Doubles once for one or more worms, excludes control/icons, and requires another 3 spice for the second VP.

grades.question: When is a normal battle-icon match checked, which cards qualify, is matching optional, and how is a wild icon used?
grades.expected: After winning and taking Conflict card face up in supply check another face-up Conflict or Objective with same icon; must flip pair face down for 1 VP. At Endgame wild can match any of three icons in supply, pair flipped for 1 VP.

observed.answer: After winning a Conflict and taking its card face up into your supply, check for a matching battle icon on another face-up Conflict or Objective card there. Matching is mandatory: flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, the wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply, flipping the pair for 1 VP.
observed.evidence: Battle Icons: when you win and take card, check another face-up Conflict or Objective; ‘must flip’; Endgame wild may match any icon.

grades.reason: Checks after taking the won card, identifies face-up Conflict/Objective eligibility, mandates flipping a normal pair for 1 VP, and handles the Endgame wild.

grades.question: What are the rewards and reversibility at 2 and 4 Faction Influence, and does tying the Alliance holder at 4 steal the Alliance?
grades.expected: Reach 2 gets 1 VP lost below 2. Reach 4 gets track bonus retained if falling below, can earn again on re-reaching. First to 4 gets Alliance and its VP; tie does not steal, opponent must rise higher. Transfer loses old holder VP and gives new holder VP.

observed.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. The first to 4 also takes the Alliance and its 1 VP; an opponent tying the holder does not take it—must rise above. If the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied player takes it (holder chooses recipient if several were tied); if holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, it returns to the board. Alliance VP follows possession.
observed.evidence: Faction Influence: 2 VP reverses below 2; 4 track bonus retained; first to 4 takes Alliance; ‘tying ... does not steal’; FAQ transfer on holder losing Influence.

grades.reason: Explains reversible 2-Influence VP, retained/repeatable 4-track bonus, first Alliance, tie retention, and possession-linked Alliance VP.

grades.question: When can Persuasion be spent during Reveal, may it be pooled or split, can you buy a Row replacement immediately, and where does the acquired card go?
grades.expected: Before between or after Reveal effects; can pool and split. Refill Row to five immediately; may buy replacement with remaining Persuasion. Acquired card face-up discard, cannot use immediately; unspent Persuasion lost.

observed.answer: Spend Persuasion during the Reveal turn before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one card and split one source across cards. The Row refills to five, so after buying a card you may buy its replacement if affordable. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile; unused Persuasion is lost.
observed.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Persuasion at any point in Reveal; pool/split; Row always five; acquired card goes face up to discard; cannot save Persuasion.

grades.reason: Allows spending before/between/after Reveal effects, pooling/splitting, buying refilled Row cards, and acquiring to face-up discard. Unspent Persuasion was not a requested subpart.

grades.question: How do Maker bonus spice, the Shield Wall and Maker Hooks affect harvesting and summoning, and where can a sandworm be placed?
grades.expected: Makers phase adds one bonus spice on each unoccupied Maker space, accumulating; visiting collects all bonus spice. Shield Wall blocks worms at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, Imperial Basin until removed to box. Maker Hooks prerequisite when specified; summoning directly bank to Conflict, never garrison.

observed.answer: At Makers, each unoccupied Maker space gains one spice on its bonus spot; when visited, you gain all accumulated bonus spice. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Hooks are required only where specified and are retained, not spent. The Shield Wall prevents summoning at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while present; once removed, worms may be summoned to any Conflict. A worm can never go into a garrison.
observed.evidence: Makers: unoccupied spaces add spice; ‘gain all’ bonus; Sandworms and Shield Wall sections give restrictions and choices.

grades.reason: The answer states one spice per unoccupied Maker space at Makers, collecting all accumulated bonus, the three protected Conflict locations, any Conflict after Wall removal, Hooks required only where specified, and never placing a worm in a garrison. The same-answer phrase "worms may be summoned to any Conflict" conveys the Conflict destination; a literal "immediately deploy" is not needed to answer where placement is permitted. The question asks where a worm can go, not which stock it comes from, so "from the bank" is not a missing requested ruling. Returning the removed Wall to the box is similarly incidental physical handling. The volunteered Deep Desert/Hagga Basin costs and spice-or-worm choices, and retained Hooks, are accurate.

grades.question: At what point does 10 VP or an empty Conflict deck end play, what happens before comparing final VP, and what are the rulebook resource tiebreakers?
grades.expected: Check in Recall at end of round, not immediately at 10 VP. Resolve Endgame Intrigue first then highest VP wins. Ties spice then Solari then water then garrisoned troops.

observed.answer: At Recall, if any player has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty, Endgame is triggered. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then highest VP wins. Resource tiebreakers in order are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
observed.evidence: Scoring: ‘At the end of a round’; first resolve Endgame Intrigue; tiebreak order spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops.

grades.reason: Checks at Recall/end of round, resolves Endgame Intrigue before VP comparison, and orders all four resource tiebreakers.

grades.question: With optional standard CHOAM, how many contracts start face up and face down, which extra cards are added, is Shaddam compulsory, and are the 10 contrasting-back contracts part of this standard setup?
grades.expected: 20 standard contracts: two face up, eighteen in bank. Add four Intrigue and four Imperium; Shaddam optional. Ten contrasting-back contracts are only Rise of Ix compatibility, excluded from standard setup.

observed.answer: Shuffle the 20 standard contracts face down, reveal two, and put the other 18 face down in the bank. Add four Intrigue and four Imperium cards to their decks. Shaddam is an optional Leader, not required. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix and stay in the box for standard CHOAM.
observed.evidence: CHOAM Setup: 20 contracts, ‘flip two face up’; shuffle 4 additional cards into each deck; Shaddam option; contrasting-back set left in box.

grades.reason: Gives two face-up/eighteen face-down standard contracts, four cards for each deck, optional Shaddam and exclusion of Ix tokens.

grades.question: Under CHOAM, what does the contract icon do, what if all contracts are taken, and how are Harvest, Immediate and Acquire The Spice Must Flow contracts completed?
grades.expected: Take one of two face-up into supply then refill face up from bank; if all taken gain 2 Solari (also without module). Harvest: visit Maker and gain specified total spice that turn including other sources. Immediate upon taking. Acquire The Spice Must Flow on next acquiring that card.

observed.answer: With CHOAM, the icon lets you take one of two face-up contracts and replace it from the bank face up; without CHOAM, or when none remain, it gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining the shown spice total that turn, including other sources. Immediate completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
observed.evidence: CHOAM Taking contracts and Completing contracts specify each completion condition.

grades.reason: Takes a selected face-up contract and refills it, gives exhausted-contract fallback, and supplies Harvest total-spice, Immediate and next-acquisition triggers. Taking the contract conveys personal possession.

grades.question: You gain a board-space contract after already sending your Agent to that space this turn. Can you complete it now? Once completed what do you announce, gain and do with the token?
grades.expected: Cannot complete now; must have held contract when Agent sent, wait future turn. Announce completion, gain printed rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

observed.answer: No. You must have held the board-space contract when sending the Agent, so a contract acquired after visiting waits until a future turn. On completion announce it, gain its rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
observed.evidence: CHOAM Completing contracts: if already sent Agent, ‘wait until a future turn’; announce, gain rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

grades.reason: Requires ownership at placement and a later visit if acquired afterward; announces, rewards, flips and retains the completed token in supply.

grades.question: In standard two-player play how many Rivals are used, who gets the Ornithopter Objective, who gets First Player, what is the turn order, and does a Rival Reveal?
grades.expected: One shared Rival. Rival gets Ornithopter Objective, other two randomly humans; Rival never First Player. Marker alternates humans, Rival considered clockwise from First Player and acts between humans each round. Takes Agent turns while it has Agent in supply, never Reveals.

observed.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. It receives the Ornithopter Objective; the humans receive the other two eligible Objectives, and the human whose card shows First Player takes the marker. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human; First Player alternates only between humans. The Rival never Reveals.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Setup: ‘one shared scoring Rival’; Rival gets Ornithopter; order listed; ‘The Rival never Reveals.’

grades.reason: Uses one Rival, assigns Ornithopter to it and remaining Objectives to humans, derives human First Player from the marked card, places Rival between humans, and denies Rival Reveal.

grades.question: A Rival reveals an occupied board space, then a Place Spy card. How does it proceed, which space costs and effects apply, and what happens when House Hagal is empty or Reshuffle is drawn?
grades.expected: Occupied: ignore and reveal again. Place Spy tries empty designated post, ignore placement if none, then reveal another card regardless because no Agent sent. Ignore normal space costs/effects; use Hagal effects only. Empty deck or Reshuffle: immediately reshuffle Hagal and continue.

observed.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of its specified type, otherwise ignore it, then immediately reveal another card either way. Ignore normal destination costs and effects; apply only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
observed.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destination and reveal again; Place Spy cards trigger another reveal; ignore normal space costs/effects; reshuffle on empty/Reshuffle.

grades.reason: Redraws occupied destinations, continues after Place Spy regardless of success, applies Hagal rather than ordinary space costs/effects, and immediately reshuffles when necessary.

grades.question: How are eligible Objective cards selected and distributed in standard three- or four-player setup, how is First Player chosen, and may Shaddam be chosen without CHOAM?
grades.expected: Omit Objectives whose 1–3P or 4/6P mark mismatches count; shuffle, each takes one random face up in supply. First Player is holder of marked Objective. Shaddam cannot be chosen without CHOAM.

observed.answer: Shuffle the Objective cards after removing those marked for a different player count; give each player one eligible Objective face up. The player whose Objective shows First Player takes the marker. Shaddam may not be used without CHOAM.
observed.evidence: Setup: omit mismatched count, shuffle eligible cards, distribute face up; Shaddam ‘Do not use ... unless playing with CHOAM.’

grades.reason: Filters mismatched Objectives, randomizes/distributes them face up, uses the marked Objective for First Player, and prohibits Shaddam without CHOAM.

grades.question: If the bank runs out of Solari, spice, water or sandworms, what happens? Contrast an empty personal troop supply, and state where resource payments go.
grades.expected: Bank resources and sandworms not limited; substitute conveniently. Cannot recruit troops from empty personal supply until returned. Resource gains come from bank and payments return to bank.

observed.answer: Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; make a convenient substitution if the bank runs out. Troops are limited by each player’s supply: if it is empty, that player cannot recruit more until troops return there. Resource gains come from the bank and payments return to the bank.
observed.evidence: Setup: resources and worms ‘not meant to be limited’; troop supply restriction; gains from bank and payments returned to it.

grades.reason: Permits substitutions for bank resources/worms, prohibits recruiting from empty personal supply, and returns resource payments to bank.

grades.question: State all five round phases in order, when Conflict and hand cards are drawn, and what Recall does if Endgame is not triggered.
grades.expected: Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. Start reveals top Conflict face up atop previous remaining cards then each draws five. If no Endgame, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise and begin next round (two-player Rival exception).

observed.answer: The phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. Round Start reveals a Conflict first, then each player draws five cards. At Recall, check for Endgame; if none, return Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and begin the next round.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure lists five phases; Round Start reveals Conflict then draws five; Recall prepares next round.

grades.reason: Orders all five phases, reveals Conflict before the five-card draw, and gives ordinary Recall/restart actions. Unasked detailed display placement is not required here.

grades.question: May you resolve board-space effects, Agent-box effects and Faction Influence in any order? Can you use that visit’s Influence to meet its entry requirement?
grades.expected: Resolve effects in any order after placement, but entry requirements and costs must be met before any effects. Cannot rely on Influence gained by the visit for its entry requirement.

observed.answer: Yes. Board-space, Agent-box, and Faction Influence effects may be resolved in any order. But all space costs and requirements must be paid/met immediately before resolving any space or played-card effects, so the visit’s Influence cannot satisfy its own entry requirement.
observed.evidence: Agent Turn: costs before resolving effects; effects may occur in any order; Faction advance listed after effects.

grades.reason: Permits post-entry effect ordering but requires all entry conditions first, so the visit cannot provide its own qualifying Influence.

grades.question: Can an optional arrow cost be paid twice in an Agent turn? Which effects are normally optional or mandatory, including costs on Intrigue cards?
grades.expected: Only once per turn, except sandworm-doubled Conflict rewards. Most effects mandatory except may, optional arrow payment and black-X trash. Direct self-trash mandatory. All Intrigue conditions/costs required to play it.
grades.source_references: Main pp9,20; FAQ p3 optional effects/paying a cost

observed.answer: Normally an arrow cost/effect can be used only once per turn, so an optional arrow cost cannot be paid twice for repeated effects. Most card and space effects are mandatory; exceptions include ‘may,’ optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play it; optional arrows can be declined, but then do not grant the effect. Doubled Conflict rewards are the exception to the once-per-turn arrow limit.
observed.evidence: Arrows: cost/effect once per turn, except doubled Conflict rewards; FAQ Mandatory effects and costs describes optional/mandatory cases.

grades.reason: Limits ordinary arrows to once, describes normal mandatory effects and optional may/arrow/black-X effects, and requires Intrigue costs/conditions. Doubled rewards are covered in answer or evidence.

grades.question: Where may a new Spy be placed, what if all your Spies are already deployed, and what if its placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type?
grades.expected: Unoccupied observation post, from supply. If none in supply may first recall one of own Spies for no effect. Specified icon must connect to post or cannot place there.

observed.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have none in supply, you may first recall one of your own Spies for no effect. If the placement effect requires a particular Agent-icon type connected to that post, you must meet it or cannot place the Spy.
observed.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy icon places on unoccupied post; if none in supply may recall one; specified Agent icon must connect.

grades.reason: Places from supply onto an empty post, permits no-benefit recall if supply is empty, and enforces any specified connected-icon restriction.

grades.question: Can you Infiltrate your own occupied board space, use a Spy without playing a card, or recall two connected Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement?
grades.expected: No to all. Infiltrate bypasses another player Agent; still play a card and meet entry costs/requirements. Two Spies can pay different effects (Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence), not duplicate Gather Intelligence.

observed.answer: No, Infiltrate bypasses only another player’s Agent, not your own. A Spy does not let you take an Agent turn by itself: ordinary Agent turn still requires playing a card. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; you may use different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Infiltrate cannot bypass own Agent; Gather Intelligence requires placement; same Spy cannot pay both; FAQ recalling Spy requires playing a card.

grades.reason: Rejects own-Agent infiltration, card-free Agent turns and duplicate intelligence; permits two Spies for distinct effects.

grades.question: Who gets control bonuses when visiting Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin, how is control transferred, and where does the defensive troop originate?
grades.expected: Winning respective Conflict puts control marker on flag replacing opponent. Controller receives 1 Solari at Arrakeen/Refinery or 1 spice at Basin whenever anyone including self visits. Reveal of controlled location Conflict permits one troop from supply directly to Conflict.

observed.answer: Whenever anyone visits a controlled location, its controller gets the bonus (1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery; 1 spice at Imperial Basin), separately from the visitor’s effects; a controller visiting also gets both. A Conflict winner at that location places a Control marker, replacing the previous one. When the Conflict is revealed for a location already controlled, its controller may deploy one troop from supply without visiting.
observed.evidence: Critical Locations: controller receives bonus whenever any player visits; winning control replaces marker; reveal defensive troop from supply.

grades.reason: Awards named visit bonuses to controller even on self-visits, replaces control on winning the location Conflict, and sources optional defense directly from supply.

grades.question: When two players tie for second in a three-player Conflict, what happens? What if players tie for third in four-player play, or three players tie for first?
grades.expected: Tied second each get third reward; winner keeps first and card, no other rewards. Tied third receive nothing. Three tied first each get second, no winner/card and no further rewards.

observed.answer: For a tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; first-place winner keeps first reward and Conflict card, and no further rewards are given. Players tied for third get nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets second reward, nobody takes the card, and no other rewards are given (including to a fourth player).
observed.evidence: Combat ties table: second tie and third tie rows; three tied first clarified as no other rewards in either 3- or 4-player game.

grades.reason: Gives tied seconds third reward while winner keeps first/card, gives tied thirds nothing, and gives three tied leaders second with no card or further rewards.

grades.question: At a normal three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, which places receive rewards? What if a two-player game’s Rival is one of the participants?
grades.expected: Only first and second rewarded, third only used for a tie for second. Two humans plus standard Rival use the same two-/three-player reward rules; Rival competes normally.
grades.source_references: Main p14; Supplements p5 Combat; FAQ p1 Conflict

observed.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three distinct positive strengths, first and second place get their rewards; third gets none. This is also true with a two-player game’s Rival as third competitor: 2–3-player reward rules apply, with the Rival counted as a player.
observed.evidence: Resolve Combat: with 2 or 3 players, ordinary first and second receive rewards; third only in a tie for second; includes Rival game.

grades.reason: Pays ordinary first and second only with three competitors, including two humans plus Rival.

grades.question: When can Plot, Combat and Endgame Intrigues be played, how are unplayed Intrigues kept and ordinary ones discarded, and what if the Intrigue deck is exhausted?
grades.expected: Plot during own Agent/Reveal turns, Combat during Combat with a unit, Endgame at game end. Unplayed face down separate from deck, owner may inspect; played resolved cards face up Intrigue discard. Exhaustion reshuffles Intrigue discard into new deck.
grades.source_references: Main p7 / extraction 345–354; FAQ p2 Intrigue cards

observed.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turns; Combat Intrigues only during Combat; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down and separate from your deck; after resolving, put them face up in the Intrigue discard pile. If the deck runs out, shuffle its discard pile into a new deck.
observed.evidence: Intrigue cards section and FAQ Draw timing: types/timing, face-down separate, face-up discard; exhausted deck is reshuffled.

grades.reason: The Plot/Endgame timing, ordinary face-up discard, separate face-down storage and exhaustion reshuffle are correct. "Only during Combat" states a necessary timing restriction, not an affirmative permission to play without units, so the defect is an omission rather than a false ruling. Unit eligibility is material to the expressly requested question of when a player can play these cards. No same-response statement supplies it; naming source sections cannot supply the missing fact. Face down and separate answers how unplayed cards are kept. Owner inspection is useful background but is not another storage state or a separately requested permission; its omission alone would not make this answer partial.

grades.question: Can you discard an Intrigue for an ordinary discard instruction? Where does an ordinary discard come from? How does Secrets choose which Intrigue is stolen?
grades.expected: Ordinary discard from hand and cannot be Intrigue unless specified. Secrets steals one random Intrigue from each opponent with four or more, in addition to drawing one from deck and gaining Bene Gesserit Influence.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1104–1106,1179–1181; Supplements p2; FAQ p2 discard

observed.answer: No, an ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand and cannot discard Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Secrets’ steal effect takes one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent who has at least four.
observed.evidence: Discarding: from hand, not Intrigue unless specified; Intrigue cards: Steal icon random from each opponent with 4+.

grades.question: What counts as in play for Fremen Bond, can two Bond cards activate one another regardless of play order, and when do they cease being in play?

observed.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: other Fremen cards in play; Bond cards can activate each other; cards remain until Clean Up.

grades.question: Can Recall Agent return the Agent placed this turn, and when can the recalled Agent act again? Where does a retreated troop go, and may “retreat any number” mean zero?
grades.expected: Recall another Agent from board to Leader, not current-turn Agent; can use on later Agent turn same round. Retreat Conflict to garrison; any number permits zero.

observed.evidence: FAQ Draw timing: during Reveal ‘immediately reveal and use’; after Reveal keep for next round; Plot stays face up until Reveal then discarded.

grades.expected: Tie for first is not a win, cannot play. An appropriate Intrigue received as winning reward can be played immediately.

observed.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops: cannot play after tying; if received as winning reward, may play immediately.

grades.question: What if final VP, spice, Solari, water and garrison troops all remain tied, and may scores exceed 12?
grades.expected: Final tiebreaker is player who most recently took Reveal turn. Scores may exceed printed track maximum 12.

grades.question: Under CHOAM does Shaddam begin with his set-aside Sardaukar contracts, when can he take one, and how long does his Signet Ring deployment restriction last?
grades.expected: No, not in possession at start. Sardaukar Commander allows acquiring set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of generally available one when taking a contract. Emperor of Known Universe restriction starts immediately with Signet Ring Agent placement and lasts that turn only.

grades.question: For Margot and Irulan does moving from 1 to 3 Influence count as reaching 2, can it trigger again later, and does descending through 2 count? Does Clean Up trigger Spacing Guild’s Favor discard ability?

grades.question: State Accept Contract and Dutiful Service’s Agent icons and effects with and without CHOAM, and whether both automatically advance a Faction track.

grades.question: What do Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station each cost and provide, what Agent icons access them, and which are Combat spaces?

grades.question: Compare Deep Desert and Hagga Basin’s entry costs, base spice and worm choices. Do you still collect bonus spice when choosing worms, and are Hooks spent?

grades.question: How do High Council’s first and subsequent visits differ, what does each cost, when is its ongoing benefit used, and is it a Combat space?

grades.question: What does Swordmaster cost before and after anyone obtains one, how often may each player visit, and when can the new Agent be used? Does a Rival obtaining it lower human cost?

grades.question: When choosing Influence, how does a Rival select the Faction and break ties? Does it get VP at 2 and Alliance VP, or the track bonus at 4? What does a numbered Hagal Influence icon mean?

When its Conflict is revealed, the existing controller may deploy one troop directly from supply to the Conflict without visiting.

grades.reason: Awards named visit bonuses to controller even on self-visits, replaces control on winning the location Conflict, and sources optional defense directly from supply.

grades.question: When two players tie for second in a three-player Conflict, what happens? What if players tie for third in four-player play, or three players tie for first?
grades.expected: Tied second each get third reward; winner keeps first and card, no other rewards. Tied third receive nothing. Three tied first each get second, no winner/card and no further rewards.

observed.answer: For a tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps first reward and the card, and no further rewards are given. Tied third-place players get nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward, nobody takes the card, and no one else gets a reward in either three- or four-player play.
observed.evidence: Tie rules table: second tied each third, winner keeps first and card; third tied get nothing; three tied first get second and “no other rewards in either a three-player or four-player game.”

grades.reason: Gives tied seconds third reward while winner keeps first/card, gives tied thirds nothing, and gives three tied leaders second with no card or further rewards.

grades.question: At a normal three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, which places receive rewards? What if a two-player game’s Rival is one of the participants?
grades.expected: Only first and second rewarded, third only used for a tie for second. Two humans plus standard Rival use the same two-/three-player reward rules; Rival competes normally.
grades.source_references: Main p14; Supplements p5 Combat; FAQ p1 Conflict

observed.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second place receive their printed rewards; third receives nothing. This is also true in a two-human game with a Rival: the Rival counts as the third competitor, and ordinary first and second are rewarded while an untied third is not.
observed.evidence: “with 2 or 3 players (including two humans plus a Rival), ordinary first and second place receive rewards, and ordinary third… nothing.”

grades.reason: Pays ordinary first and second only with three competitors, including two humans plus Rival.

grades.question: When can Plot, Combat and Endgame Intrigues be played, how are unplayed Intrigues kept and ordinary ones discarded, and what if the Intrigue deck is exhausted?
grades.expected: Plot during own Agent/Reveal turns, Combat during Combat with a unit, Endgame at game end. Unplayed face down separate from deck, owner may inspect; played resolved cards face up Intrigue discard. Exhaustion reshuffles Intrigue discard into new deck.
grades.source_references: Main p7 / extraction 345–354; FAQ p2 Intrigue cards

observed.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played on your own Agent or Reveal turns; Combat Intrigues only during Combat; Endgame Intrigues only at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, and reveal only when played; after resolution put them face up in an Intrigue discard pile. If the Intrigue Deck runs out, shuffle its discard pile into a new deck.
observed.evidence: Intrigue section lists timing by type and storage/discard; FAQ: if Intrigue deck runs out, “shuffle its discard to form a new deck.”

grades.reason: The phase labels, face-down separate storage, face-up ordinary discard, and exhaustion reshuffle are correct. "Only during Combat" does not affirmatively permit play without units, so this is incomplete rather than false. The unit condition determines whether the player can use the requested play window and is material. No statement in the answer or its evidence supplies that condition. "Reveal only when played" ordinarily means reveal to opponents; it does not prohibit the owner privately inspecting a face-down card. I therefore find no inspection contradiction and do not separately demand that unasked inspection permission merely to answer storage.

grades.question: Can you discard an Intrigue for an ordinary discard instruction? Where does an ordinary discard come from? How does Secrets choose which Intrigue is stolen?
grades.expected: Ordinary discard from hand and cannot be Intrigue unless specified. Secrets steals one random Intrigue from each opponent with four or more, in addition to drawing one from deck and gaining Bene Gesserit Influence.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1104–1106,1179–1181; Supplements p2; FAQ p2 discard

observed.answer: No, an ordinary discard instruction cannot discard an Intrigue unless it says so. An ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand, not a card in play or discard pile. Secrets steals one Intrigue chosen at random from each opponent who has at least four Intrigues.
observed.evidence: Discarding: choose a card “from your hand”; “It cannot be an Intrigue card unless specified”; Secrets: each opponent with 4+ gives one “selected at random.”

grades.reason: Requires ordinary non-Intrigue discard from hand unless specified and chooses one stolen Intrigue randomly from each 4+ opponent. Other Secrets visit effects were not asked.

grades.question: Which cards may a trash effect remove, where do ordinary and Reserve cards go, and is trashing optional? Does trashing The Spice Must Flow remove its acquired VP?
grades.expected: May trash own hand, discard or in-play card. Ordinary to box; Reserve back to its Reserve stack. Optional unless cost or direct self-trash. The Spice Must Flow acquire VP retained after trashing.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1185–1190; FAQ p4 The Spice Must Flow

observed.answer: Trash effects can remove cards from your hand, discard pile, or in play; ordinary trashed cards go to the box, while Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or the card instructs you to trash itself. The VP gained from The Spice Must Flow's acquire effect remains even if you later trash that card.
observed.evidence: Trash from hand, discard or in play; “Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack”; optional except costs/self; FAQ says acquire VP “is retained if the card is later trashed.”

grades.reason: Covers hand/discard/in-play trash sources, box versus Reserve destinations, optionality exceptions, and retention of acquired Spice Must Flow VP.

grades.question: When do acquire-box effects resolve, when do you reshuffle your deck, and can unused Persuasion be carried to another round?
grades.expected: Acquire effect once at acquisition not when later played. Reshuffle discard only when unable to draw due to empty deck then continue. Unspent Reveal Persuasion lost, never saved.

observed.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once at the moment the card is acquired, not when later played. If you cannot draw because your deck is empty, reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. Persuasion not used during your Reveal turn is lost and cannot be carried forward.
observed.evidence: Acquire box effect occurs “at the moment you acquire”; reshuffle discard when deck empty; unused Persuasion “is lost.”

grades.reason: Resolves acquire effects once at acquisition, reshuffles on a needed draw from empty deck, and loses unused Persuasion.

grades.question: What counts as in play for Fremen Bond, can two Bond cards activate one another regardless of play order, and when do they cease being in play?
grades.expected: Agent-turn and Reveal cards remain in play face up until Reveal Clean Up unless trashed earlier. Bond requires at least one other Fremen in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of order.

observed.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed during Reveal remain face up and in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond may use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards may activate each other regardless of play order. They cease being in play at Clean Up when moved to discard.
observed.evidence: “Cards you play on Agent turns and reveal… remain face up and ‘in play’ until… Clean Up”; “two Fremen Bond cards can activate one another, regardless of order.”

grades.reason: Includes Agent/Reveal cards in play until cleanup unless trashed, requires another Fremen, and permits mutual Bond regardless of order.

grades.question: Can Recall Agent return the Agent placed this turn, and when can the recalled Agent act again? Where does a retreated troop go, and may “retreat any number” mean zero?
grades.expected: Recall another Agent from board to Leader, not current-turn Agent; can use on later Agent turn same round. Retreat Conflict to garrison; any number permits zero.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1147–1157; FAQ p3 Retreat

observed.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent you just sent; the recalled Agent can be used again on a later Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop goes from Conflict back to your garrison. “Retreat any number” can mean zero troops.
observed.evidence: Recall Agent returns “one of your other Agents”; can “use it again on another Agent turn in the same round”; retreat moves troop to garrison; FAQ says “any number” allows zero.

grades.reason: Recalls another board Agent for later same-round use, retreats Conflict troops to garrison, and permits retreating zero.

grades.question: When an effect grants two Influence with a freely chosen Faction, may it be split? What is required for an Alliance-icon effect or a minimum-Influence effect?
grades.expected: Choose one Faction, both Influence there (not split). Alliance effect requires holding shown Faction Alliance token; minimum-Influence effect requires at least shown value with shown Faction.

observed.answer: For a free-choice Influence effect that grants two, choose one Faction and gain both there; you cannot split the two across Factions. An Alliance icon requires you to hold that Faction's Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires the specified minimum with that Faction.
observed.evidence: Free-choice gain-two: “you can't choose two different Factions”; Alliance icon “requires you to hold” token; some card effects require minimum Influence.

grades.reason: Puts a single two-Influence effect entirely in one Faction and supplies Alliance-token and minimum-Influence eligibility.

grades.question: If an Alliance holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, who receives the token? If the holder drops to 3 and no one has 4, what happens?
grades.expected: Former holder chooses one of previously tied opponents to receive token; holder loses Alliance VP and receiver gains it. Below 4 loses token; if no eligible 4+ player return token to board, losing its VP.

observed.answer: If the Alliance holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; if two opponents were tied, the former holder chooses which one receives it. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more, return the token to the board and the former holder loses its 1 VP.
observed.evidence: FAQ: previously tied opponent takes; “if several were tied, the former holder chooses its recipient”; at 3 or lower with nobody at 4+, token returns and old holder loses VP.

grades.reason: Lets former holder choose among formerly tied opponents and returns token to board with VP loss when no one qualifies at 4+.

grades.question: What happens to a card drawn during Reveal compared with one drawn after Reveal? What happens to a Plot Intrigue played earlier whose effect applies at Reveal?
grades.expected: During Reveal immediately reveal and use this turn; after Reveal keep until next round, then draw five extra. Plot effect for later Reveal stays face up until that Reveal, use then discard.

observed.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is revealed and used immediately that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, when you draw five additional cards. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until that effect is used, then is discarded.
observed.evidence: FAQ: “Drawn during Reveal means immediately reveal and use this turn. Drawn after Reveal means keep it for next round”; Plot with later Reveal effect “stays face up until then, is used, then discarded.”

grades.reason: Uses a during-Reveal draw immediately, retains after-Reveal draws in addition to next five, and preserves delayed Plot until its Reveal effect then discards.

grades.question: May a “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue be played after tying for first? What if you receive such an Intrigue as a reward for an outright win?
grades.expected: Tie for first is not a win, cannot play. An appropriate Intrigue received as winning reward can be played immediately.
grades.source_references: FAQ p4 When you win a Conflict

observed.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first, because no one wins. If you receive such an Intrigue as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
observed.evidence: FAQ: “‘When you win a Conflict’ Intrigues cannot be played after tying for first; if received as a winning reward they can be played immediately.”

grades.reason: Rejects win-trigger Intrigue after tied first and allows an appropriate newly awarded Intrigue immediately after outright victory.

grades.question: What if final VP, spice, Solari, water and garrison troops all remain tied, and may scores exceed 12?
grades.expected: Final tiebreaker is player who most recently took Reveal turn. Scores may exceed printed track maximum 12.
grades.source_references: FAQ p2 Endgame; p4 Victory Points

observed.answer: If VP, spice, Solari, water, and garrisoned troops all tie, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed 12.
observed.evidence: FAQ: “If all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track’s 12.”

grades.reason: Uses most recent Reveal as final tiebreaker and permits scores above 12.

grades.question: Can you delay completion of two held contracts for the same board space after visiting, and when in the Agent turn can their effects resolve?
grades.expected: Completion mandatory; all same-space contracts completed with one Agent placement. Their effects may resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects; still must hold them at placement.

observed.answer: No. You must complete every held contract for that space with that one Agent placement; you cannot delay them to a later turn. They are another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects, provided you held them when placing the Agent.
observed.evidence: FAQ: “Fulfill all contracts you hold for the same space with one Agent placement”; completion is another effect that “can resolve in any order”; must hold at placement.

grades.reason: Requires all held same-space contracts to complete on the visit and allows their effects in any order with other Agent-turn effects.

grades.question: Under CHOAM does Shaddam begin with his set-aside Sardaukar contracts, when can he take one, and how long does his Signet Ring deployment restriction last?
grades.expected: No, not in possession at start. Sardaukar Commander allows acquiring set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of generally available one when taking a contract. Emperor of Known Universe restriction starts immediately with Signet Ring Agent placement and lasts that turn only.
grades.source_references: Main p17; FAQ p3 Shaddam Corrino IV

observed.answer: Shaddam does not begin with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts; they are not initially in his possession. With his Sardaukar Commander ability, when taking a contract he may choose a set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of a generally available one. His Emperor of the Known Universe restriction starts immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the full round.
observed.evidence: FAQ: Sardaukar contracts “do not start in your possession”; may choose one when acquiring contract; deployment restriction “takes effect immediately… lasts only for that turn.”

grades.reason: Denies initial ownership of set-aside contracts, permits substitution when acquiring, and starts the Signet restriction immediately for that turn only.

grades.question: For Feyd, where does the Training token start and what happens at its last space? Which Jessica side begins face up and can Reverend Mother Jessica act on the flip turn?
grades.expected: Feyd starts leftmost Training space, stays forever on rightmost once reached. Lady Jessica side starts up, not Reverend Mother. Reverend Mother ability usable on flip turn.
grades.source_references: Main p17 / extraction 957–964; FAQ p3 Reverend Mother Jessica

observed.answer: Feyd's token starts at the leftmost Training-track space and stays at the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica begins with her Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
observed.evidence: Leader clarifications state Feyd token placement and remaining at rightmost; “Lady Jessica… begin… Lady Jessica side face up”; FAQ says Reverend Mother Jessica may use ability on flip turn.

grades.reason: Starts Feyd leftmost and retains him at the final space; starts Lady Jessica side up and permits Reverend Mother ability on flip turn.

grades.question: For Margot and Irulan does moving from 1 to 3 Influence count as reaching 2, can it trigger again later, and does descending through 2 count? Does Clean Up trigger Spacing Guild’s Favor discard ability?
grades.expected: Passing 2 upward counts, can repeat by losing then regaining Influence; descending does not count. Spacing Guild Favor triggers discard from hand, not in-play-to-discard Clean Up.

observed.answer: For Margot and Irulan, moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2, so the effect triggers. It can trigger again later by losing Influence and then moving up through/reaching 2 again; descending through 2 does not count as reaching it. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
observed.evidence: Clarification: you reach 2 moving past 2 with multiple Influence; can reach it again after losing and regaining, only when moving up; Guild's Favor Clean Up does not trigger discard ability.

grades.reason: Counts upward passage through 2, permits repeated upward reaches, excludes downward passage, and rejects cleanup as the Guild Favor discard trigger.

grades.question: State Accept Contract and Dutiful Service’s Agent icons and effects with and without CHOAM, and whether both automatically advance a Faction track.
grades.expected: Accept Contract: Spice Trade, draw card plus contract or 2 Solari, no automatic Faction Influence. Dutiful Service: Emperor, one Emperor Influence plus contract or 2 Solari. Contract fallback if module off or all contracts taken.

observed.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon, has no cost, and always draws one card; with CHOAM it also takes a contract, while without CHOAM—or when no contracts remain—it gives 2 Solari instead. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor icon, has no cost, gains 1 Emperor Influence, and likewise takes a contract with CHOAM or 2 Solari without it/when none remain. Accept Contract is not a Faction and gives no automatic Influence; Dutiful Service gives one Emperor Influence once total (its listed effect is the same as the Faction advance, not an extra one).
observed.evidence: Board guide: Accept Contract is Spice Trade, no cost, always draw; CHOAM contract/otherwise 2 Solari. Dutiful Service is Emperor, gains 1 Emperor Influence and contract/otherwise 2 Solari. Faction clarification: Accept is non-Faction; Dutiful's one Influence counted once.

grades.reason: The answer states each icon, Accept Contract always drawing a card, the module alternatives for both spaces, no automatic Faction advance for Accept Contract, and one total Emperor Influence for Dutiful Service. It also explicitly states depletion fallback for each, leaving no gap even on a broader effects reading. The volunteered no-cost claims agree with the guide. "Accept Contract is not a Faction" reasonably means it is not a Faction space in context; requiring that exact noun phrase would force literal matching without changing the conveyed rule.

grades.question: What do Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station each cost and provide, what Agent icons access them, and which are Combat spaces?
grades.expected: Arrakeen City free, troop and card, controller 1 Solari. Fremkit Fremen free, 1 Fremen Influence and card. Research Station City 2 water, two troops and two cards. All Combat.

observed.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat space; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, and the controller separately gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat space; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat space; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
observed.evidence: Board guide rows list Arrakeen City/Yes/no cost; Fremkit Fremen/Yes/no cost; Research Station City/Yes/2 water.

grades.reason: Supplies all three access icons, entry costs, recruits/draws/Influence/controller effects and positive Combat flags.

grades.question: Compare Deep Desert and Hagga Basin’s entry costs, base spice and worm choices. Do you still collect bonus spice when choosing worms, and are Hooks spent?
grades.expected: Deep Desert 3 water, 4 spice OR two worms; Hagga 1 water, 2 spice OR one worm. Both collect all bonus spice even with worms. Worm choice requires Maker Hooks, not spent; cannot summon into Shield-Wall-protected Conflict.
grades.source_references: Supplements pp1–2; Main p10; FAQ p2 Maker hooks

observed.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or two sandworms if you have Maker Hooks. Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or one sandworm if you have Hooks. Visiting either also gives all accumulated bonus spice, including when you choose worms. Hooks are retained and not spent when summoning.
observed.evidence: Board guide gives costs and base/worm options; Maker rules say a visit gains “all the bonus spice”; Hooks “are never spent to summon.”

grades.reason: Correctly contrasts 3-water/4-spice/two-worm Deep Desert with 1-water/2-spice/one-worm Hagga, retains bonus spice and does not spend Hooks.

grades.question: For each Sietch Tabr option, state requirements and effects. Do you get a troop when choosing to remove the Shield Wall?
grades.expected: City access, 2+ Fremen Influence, no resource cost. Option one Hooks if needed, one troop, one water; option two one water and may remove wall. Option two gives no troop or Hooks. Combat space.

observed.answer: Both Sietch Tabr choices require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit one troop, and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second choice gives no troop.
observed.evidence: Sietch Tabr row: “City… No resource cost; 2+ Fremen Influence”; choose Hooks + recruit + water, or water + optionally remove Wall.

grades.reason: Applies City/2+ Fremen/no-resource-cost entry to both exclusive options and correctly excludes a troop from Wall removal.

grades.question: How do High Council’s first and subsequent visits differ, what does each cost, when is its ongoing benefit used, and is it a Combat space?
grades.expected: Landsraad 5 Solari each visit. First Councilor to empty seat, +2 Persuasion each Reveal rest of game; later 2 spice, Intrigue, three troops. Not Combat, cannot normally deploy recruited troops.

observed.answer: High Council is a Landsraad, non-Combat space. Each visit costs 5 Solari. On your first visit, place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Subsequent visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
observed.evidence: High Council row: Landsraad/No; 5 Solari each visit; first visit grants ongoing 2 Persuasion every Reveal; subsequent visit rewards listed.

grades.reason: Charges 5 Solari each visit, distinguishes Councilor/ongoing Reveal Persuasion from later spice/Intrigue/troops, and marks non-Combat.

grades.question: What does Swordmaster cost before and after anyone obtains one, how often may each player visit, and when can the new Agent be used? Does a Rival obtaining it lower human cost?
grades.expected: Landsraad 8 Solari before any Swordmaster, then 6; once per player per game. Third Agent from beside board onto Leader immediately usable same round and rest of game. Rival also lowers cost.

observed.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains one and 6 Solari once anyone has one. Each player may visit/gain the Swordmaster only once per game. The third Agent is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining Swordmaster also lowers the human cost to 6 Solari.
observed.evidence: Swordmaster row: “8 Solari before anyone gains Swordmaster; 6 once anyone has one”; once per player; available this round and rest of game; Rival gaining also reduces human cost.

grades.reason: Charges 8 then 6 including Rival ownership, limits to once per player, and makes the Agent usable this round and thereafter.

grades.question: State Imperial Privilege’s Agent icon, requirement, entry cost and effects. Which Agent can it recall and does it automatically give Emperor Influence?
grades.expected: Landsraad, 2+ Emperor Influence, 3 Solari. May discard Intrigue to draw Intrigue; recall another Agent and draw card. Not the current Agent. No automatic Emperor Influence.

observed.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access; it requires 2+ Emperor Influence and costs 3 Solari. Its effects let you discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, and recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence and can recall only another Agent, not the one just placed.
observed.evidence: Imperial Privilege row: Landsraad; 3 Solari, 2+ Emperor; may discard Intrigue for one, recall one of your other Agents and draw; Landsraad is not a Faction.

grades.reason: Gives Landsraad, 2+ Emperor, 3 Solari, optional Intrigue exchange, another-Agent recall and draw, with no automatic Emperor Influence.

grades.question: State Shipping’s access icon, Influence requirement, cost and gains. Does its free-choice Influence have to be with the Guild?
grades.expected: Spice Trade, 2+ Guild Influence, 3 spice. Gain 5 Solari and one Influence any one Faction, not necessarily Guild.

observed.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and costs 3 spice. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction, which need not be the Guild.
observed.evidence: Shipping row lists Spice Trade; 3 spice and 2+ Guild; “Gain 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction.”

grades.reason: Gives Spice Trade, 2+ Guild and 3 spice, gains 5 Solari and freely chosen single Influence, which need not be Guild.

grades.question: Compare Gather Support and Spice Refinery’s zero-cost and paid options and Combat status.
grades.expected: Gather Support Landsraad choose 0/2 Solari, two troops either way, plus one water if paid, not Combat. Refinery City choose 0/1 spice, gain 2/4 Solari respectively, controller 1 Solari either way, Combat.

observed.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad and not a Combat space: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit two troops either way, and if you pay 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City and a Combat space: choose to pay 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari for free or 4 Solari if you pay 1 spice; its controller separately gains 1 Solari.
observed.evidence: Guide rows: Gather Support Landsraad/No with 0-or-2 Solari options; Spice Refinery City/Yes with 0-or-1 spice and 2-or-4 Solari, plus controller bonus.

grades.reason: Covers both paid/free alternatives and Combat flags, including Refinery controller bonus.

grades.question: State Heighliner, Desert Tactics and Sardaukar’s entry costs, Influence gains, recruits and other effects; which allow normal deployment?
grades.expected: Heighliner 5 spice, Guild Influence +1 and five troops, Combat. Desert Tactics 1 water, Fremen Influence +1 and one troop, optional trash, Combat. Sardaukar 4 spice, Emperor Influence +1 and four troops plus Intrigue, not Combat.

observed.answer: Heighliner costs 5 spice, grants 1 Spacing Guild Influence and recruits five troops; it is a Combat space, so normal deployment is allowed. Desert Tactics costs 1 water, grants 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop, and optionally trashes a card; it is a Combat space. Sardaukar costs 4 spice, grants 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits four troops; it is not a Combat space, so normal deployment is not allowed there.
observed.evidence: Board guide lists Heighliner Guild/Yes/5 spice and five recruits; Desert Tactics Fremen/Yes/1 water, Influence, troop and optional trash; Sardaukar Emperor/No/4 spice, Influence, Intrigue, four troops.

grades.reason: Gives all three entry costs, Influence, troop quantities and extra effects and permits normal deployment only at Heighliner/Desert Tactics.

grades.question: What are Assembly Hall, Espionage and Deliver Supplies’s Agent icons, costs and effects, including Assembly Hall’s timing condition?
grades.expected: Assembly Hall Landsraad free, Intrigue now, 1 Persuasion at Reveal if own Agent there. Espionage BG 1 spice, 1 BG Influence, card and Spy. Deliver Supplies Guild free, 1 Guild Influence and 1 water. None Combat.

observed.answer: Assembly Hall uses Landsraad access, has no entry cost and is non-Combat; draw an Intrigue, and if your Agent is there gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn. Espionage uses Bene Gesserit access, costs 1 spice, is non-Combat, and gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, a card draw, and a Spy placement. Deliver Supplies uses Spacing Guild access, has no cost, is non-Combat, and gives 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
observed.evidence: The three Board Space Guide rows list these icons, costs, Combat status and effects; Assembly Hall's Persuasion is conditional on Agent still being there at Reveal.

grades.reason: Gives all three icons/costs/effects and conditions Assembly Hall Persuasion on the Agent being there at Reveal.

grades.question: What must False Orders’ affected opponents do, may it be played without an opposing Spy connected to your destination, and when is Litany Against Fear’s red box ignored?
grades.expected: Each affected opponent moves Spy to empty observation post not connected to this turn Agent destination. Can play without enemy Spy there. Litany red box ignored during Reveal or with gained Agent icon when played normally as Agent card.
grades.source_references: FAQ pp2–3 False Orders/Litany Against Fear

observed.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. It may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when the card gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
observed.evidence: FAQ: False Orders' affected opponents move Spy to an empty post “not connected to your Agent’s destination”; may play without an enemy Spy; Litany red box ignored in Reveal or normal Agent play.

grades.reason: Requires an empty non-connected Spy destination, permits False Orders without an enemy Spy, and gives both Litany red-box exceptions.

grades.question: With Manipulate, may opponents acquire the removed card, may you acquire it by other means with the discount, and when does an unacquired card leave the game?
grades.expected: Opponents cannot acquire. You may use other means but 1-Persuasion discount does not apply. If not acquired by end of next Reveal turn, remove from game.

observed.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it is still unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
observed.evidence: FAQ: “opponents cannot acquire the removed card”; you may acquire by other means “without the 1-Persuasion discount”; otherwise remove at end of next Reveal.

grades.reason: Excludes opponents, permits other acquisition means without discount, and removes the unacquired card at next Reveal end.

grades.question: What components and resource does the standard two-player Rival start with, what happens to the 2P Reshuffle card, and can its 10 VP trigger Endgame and victory?
grades.expected: Four cubes at Influence bottoms, three garrison troops rest supply, two Agents supply and third beside board, three Spies and one water supply, score/Combat zero. Retain Reshuffle in Hagal. Scoring Rival can trigger end at 10+ and win.

observed.answer: The standard Rival starts with four cubes on the bottoms of Influence tracks, three troops in its garrison and the rest in supply, two Agents in supply with Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies, and 1 water; score and Combat markers start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and put it near the Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival is a scoring competitor: its 10+ VP can trigger Endgame and it can win.
